topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, sets the framework for the cancer lecture series, and outlines the main learning outcomes regarding environmental exposures, carcinogenicity methodologies, and initiation versus promotion.

topics.label: Biological Nature of Cancer and Sources of Mutation Accumulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer evolves through somatic mutation accumulation and permissive microenvironments, driven by a combination of endogenous cellular processes, inherited risks, and extrinsic factors.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence for Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine various environmental carcinogens, address public debate around cancer being driven by bad luck versus preventable causes, and evaluate geographic epidemiological patterns to disentangle environmental from genetic influences.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens as Drivers of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, detailing the epidemiology, co-factors, and cellular mechanisms underlying Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Carcinogen Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical agents undergo xenobiotic metabolic processing to generate reactive derivatives, oxidative stress, and bulky DNA adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammatory Microenvironments, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters and chronic inflammation drive clonal expansion alongside initiating mutations, while evaluating the influence of host developmental stages and tissue specificity.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the laboratory and population-level methodologies used to determine carcinogenicity, including whole-genome mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo toxicological models, and the in vitro Ames test.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes with a closing reflection on everyday risk-versus-benefit tradeoffs of carcinogen exposure and a summary of key lecture themes.
